name: ttf-parser
language: Rust (basic C API in c-api/, benchmark harness is C++)
baseline: FreeType (FT_Load_Glyph with FT_LOAD_NO_SCALE plus FT_Outline_Decompose); stb_truetype also measured
workload: Time to extract the outlines of all glyphs in a test font, per outline table type (glyf, gvar, CFF, CFF2), using a Google Benchmark C++ harness that calls FreeType, stb_truetype and ttf-parser through its C API.
claimed_speedup: AMD 3700X: glyf 0.901 ms vs FreeType 1.171 ms (~1.3x, derived from page data); gvar 2.972 vs 4.132 ms (~1.4x); CFF 1.197 vs 5.647 ms (~4.7x); CFF2 1.968 vs 6.392 ms (~3.2x). Apple M1: glyf 0.550 vs 0.854 ms (~1.6x); gvar 2.270 vs 4.594 ms (~2.0x); CFF 1.054 vs 5.223 ms (~5.0x); CFF2 1.765 vs 5.995 ms (~3.4x). stb_truetype is faster than ttf-parser on glyf on x86 (0.675 ms).
compiler_and_flags: Numbers table does not state a compiler or flags. The public harness (benches/outline/meson.build) builds C++14 with meson --buildtype release, links FreeType >= 2.8 and stb_truetype, and the C API is built with cargo build --release.
hardware: AMD 3700X (x86) and Apple M1 (ARM), as listed in the v0.20.0 README
tradeoffs: Parser and outliner only: no rasterization, no hinting, no shaping (it is the parsing layer under rusttype, ab-glyph and fontdue style renderers). Zero heap allocation, no unsafe, no dependencies. C++ callers must go through the basic C API (c-api/ttfparser.h, cbindgen output hand-edited) and need a Rust toolchain to build it. At v0.20.0 COLR and CPAL were v0 only and some bitmap table formats were unsupported.
caveats: The numbers come from the v0.20.0 README; the current README no longer carries the table and says the crate is in maintenance mode (bug fixes only, performance work not accepted, fontations recommended instead). The author's own note under the table: FreeType is surprisingly slow and he worries he may have measured it wrongly. The benchmark measures outline extraction with FT_LOAD_NO_SCALE, not rendering or hinting, so it is not an end-to-end FreeType comparison. Compiler version is not stated, so this stays at tier C although the harness code is public. On x86 glyf, stb_truetype beats ttf-parser. Primary language is Rust, so fit with the C++ language filter is partial (usable from C++ via the C API, and the benchmark itself is C++). The repo moved from RazrFalcon/ttf-parser to harfbuzz/ttf-parser; the v0.20.0 page was read at the old owner path.
found_via: WebSearch 'font subsetting OR font parsing C OR C++ library "faster than" fonttools OR FreeType benchmark github' surfaced the crate; then read the current README, CONTRIBUTING.md, benches/outline/{README.md,meson.build,outline.cc} and the v0.20.0 README raw file

name: uni-algo
baseline: ICU (word break and extended grapheme cluster break iteration over UTF-16 text)
workload: Unicode text segmentation (UAX #29 word breaks and extended grapheme cluster breaks) over a 'real text' sample in UTF-16, five consecutive runs per configuration.
claimed_speedup: MSVC 19.12 x64, first run: word breaks 2355.47 (uni-algo) vs 11379.4 (ICU), ~4.8x; grapheme breaks 2067.16 vs 5600.95, ~2.7x. MSVC 19.12 x86: word breaks 2544.55 vs 13137.1, ~5.2x; grapheme breaks 2239.48 vs 6766.44, ~3.0x (ratios derived from page data; units are not stated, lower is assumed better).
compiler_and_flags: MSVC 19.12 (Visual Studio 2017 15.5.5), x64 and x86, flags not stated; GCC 7.3 -O3 rows exist but the ICU column is 0 there (ICU not built under MinGW)
tradeoffs: Header-only C++17 library with optional compiled Unicode data, UTF-8/16/32 support and safe iterators with bounds checks in debug. The README lists the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm and the Line Breaking Algorithm as planned for future versions, so it does not yet cover bidi or line breaking, only word and grapheme segmentation (plus case, normalization and collation). Dual licensed Public Domain or MIT.
caveats: Category fit is weak: the benchmarked task is Unicode segmentation, a pre-step of text layout, not font shaping or rasterization, and the baseline is ICU rather than HarfBuzz or FreeType. Results use 2018-era toolchains (GCC 7.3, MSVC 2017), and the perf commits date from April 2023. The result file states no units, no CPU model, no ICU version and no description of the text sample; ICU was measured only under MSVC. The author calls his own perf test 'a mess', and the README claims only performance 'at least the same as other implementations'. Only the UTF-16 segmentation test exists because ICU cluster breaks do not support UTF-8.
found_via: WebSearch 'bidi line break grapheme library C benchmark faster than ICU FriBidi github' surfaced the repo; then read README (Performance section), perf/main.cpp and perf/result/segment_utf16.md
